title: 3 Signs of a Phishing Email
points: Urgent threat: 'Account locked in 24h!'
Sender domain is almost right: paypa1.com
Link text differs from the real URL (hover first)
caption:
Phishing still works because it plays with panic. Slow down, check the sender domain, hover over links before clicking.

Save this for the next suspicious email.

title: What is IDOR?
points: IDOR = Insecure Direct Object Reference
App trusts an ID you send: /invoice?id=1001
Change it to 1002 and see someone else's data
Fix: check ownership on the server, every request
Follow for more web security basics
caption:
IDOR is one of the most common bugs in bug bounty reports. The server must verify that the logged-in user owns the object, not just that the ID exists.

Educational only. Test only systems you have permission to test.

title: Nmap: 5 Commands for Beginners
points: nmap -sV host  (service versions)
nmap -p- host  (all 65535 ports)
nmap -sC -sV host  (default scripts)
nmap -O host  (OS guess, needs root)
nmap --script vuln host  (vuln scripts)
caption:
Nmap is the first tool in most pentests. Learn these five and you can map most targets.

Use only on your own lab or systems you have written permission to scan.

title: Password Myths vs Facts
points: Myth: P@ssw0rd! is strong. Fact: it is in every wordlist
Length beats complexity: 4 random words win
Never reuse a password across sites
Use a password manager + 2FA
caption: Attackers use wordlists with common substitutions, so clever-looking passwords fall fast. Use a manager and unique passphrases.

title: XSS in 20 Seconds
points: XSS = Cross-Site Scripting
Site shows your input without cleaning it
Attacker input runs as JavaScript in the victim's browser
Can steal sessions, act as the user
Fix: output encoding + Content Security Policy
Follow for more
caption:
XSS happens when user input is rendered as code. Encode output for the right context and add a strong CSP as a second layer.

Educational only.

title: 5 Free Places to Practice Hacking Legally
points: PortSwigger Web Security Academy
TryHackMe (free rooms)
picoCTF
OverTheWire wargames
Hack The Box (free tier)
caption:
You do not need to attack real websites to learn. These platforms give you legal targets and guided practice.

Which one are you starting with?

title: Stop SQL Injection
points: Bad: build queries with string concatenation
Good: parameterized queries / prepared statements
Use an ORM correctly, never raw user input
Least-privilege database user
Validate input, but do not rely on it alone
caption: SQL injection is old but still alive. Parameterized queries remove the root cause: user data can never become SQL code.

title: Is Public Wi-Fi Safe?
points: Most sites use HTTPS, so content is encrypted
Risk: fake hotspots with the same name
Risk: captive portals asking for logins
Safer: use your phone hotspot or a trusted VPN
Turn off auto-connect to open networks
caption: Public Wi-Fi is less scary than it was, but evil-twin hotspots are real. Verify the network name with staff, and avoid logging in to banking on unknown networks.

title: Burp Suite: 4 Tabs to Learn First
points: Proxy: intercept and edit requests
Repeater: resend one request and tweak it
Intruder: automate payloads (rate-limited in Community)
Decoder: Base64, URL, hex in one click
caption:
Burp Suite is the web pentester's daily driver. Start with Proxy and Repeater, they cover most beginner bug hunting.

Use only on targets you are authorised to test.

title: Bug Bounty Roadmap for Beginners
points: 1. Networking + HTTP basics
2. OWASP Top 10 with PortSwigger labs
3. Learn Burp Suite and Linux
4. Read public write-ups daily
5. Start with VDPs, then paid programs
caption:
No shortcuts here, but there is a clear path. Fundamentals first, then labs, then real programs.

Save this and follow for the details of each step.

title: Not All 2FA is Equal
points: SMS codes: better than nothing, but SIM swap exists
Authenticator apps: better
Passkeys / hardware keys: best, phishing-resistant
Turn it on for email first, it resets everything else
caption: If your email is hacked, every account is at risk. Protect it with the strongest 2FA you can use, ideally a passkey or security key.

title: HTTP Status Codes Pentesters Watch
points: 401 = not logged in, 403 = logged in but not allowed
302 = redirect (check where it goes)
500 = server error, may leak stack traces
429 = rate limiting exists
200 on something it should block? Investigate
caption: Status codes tell you how the server thinks. A 403 that becomes 200 with a small change is often a bug.

title: Spot a Fake Link in 5 Seconds
points: Read the domain right to left before the first /
bank.com.login-check.xyz is NOT bank.com
Beware lookalike letters: rn vs m, 0 vs o
Shortened links hide the target, preview them
When unsure, type the site yourself
caption: The real domain is the part right before the first single slash. Everything before it is just a subdomain.

title: What is a CVE?
points: CVE = Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures
A public ID for one known security flaw
Example format: CVE-2021-44228
CVSS score shows severity from 0 to 10
Patch fast when a CVE hits your software
caption: CVEs give everyone the same name for the same bug. Check NVD for details, and always keep your software updated.
